body: claimed: research-agent · 2026-11-17T22:13Z · no branch · plan: research

Research answers, part 1: questions 2 and 3 (products and sources).

**Question 2: CloudCuts.**
- No product with the exact name "CloudCuts" exists in the public search results.
- The closest product is "CloudCut" (cloudcut.cam). I do not claim that this is the product the maintainer meant.
- Public page behaviour of CloudCut: it runs in a browser. It reads sheet-goods designs from Onshape, SketchUp and Fusion 360.
- It makes toolpaths without manual operation setup: profile, adaptive clearing, pockets, drilling and boring, automatic dogbones, automatic tabs.
- It nests by true shape, with rotation and interlocking. A part can be locked to a grain direction or can rotate freely.
- Extra parts move to new sheets. A live material yield figure shows.
- It sets speed, feed, plunge, stepover, depth per pass and chipload from a material and tool library. It uses the flute count, diameter and coating of the bit.
- A changed model that is imported again rebuilds the full job.
- The vendor says that it posts to more than 800 routers. This claim is not verified.
- The page does not describe tool changes or the drilling strategy.
- Source: https://cloudcut.cam/

**Question 3: other router products (behaviour only).**
- Mozaik CNC: true-shape nesting, automatic tabs, onion skin and return skin, stay-down toolpaths for small parts, joint fastener drilling, nested part labels, a remnant library, spoilboard surfacing. https://www.mozaiksoftware.com/products/mozaik-cnc
- Thermwood cabinet nesting release notes: drill banks, 32 mm and 64 mm line bores, tab insert and delete, arc tabs, drilling of tabs, part priority by job, cabinet and item, vacuum zones through machine code, pre- and post-tool-change macros. https://www.thermwood.com/updates_control_nesting_home.htm
- SigmaNEST router page: Z-depth tabs, 3D tabs, onion skin, gang drill recognition, custom tool order, spiral-inward cutting for vacuum hold-down, Z-ramp and contour lead-ins, small part handling. https://www.sigmateksystems.com/en/supported-machine-types/router
- SWOOD Nesting: grain per material, fixed or limited rotation in 90 degree steps, labels with barcodes, remnant tracking, tabs with user size, position and number. https://www.goengineer.com/swood/nesting
- Vectric VCarve: tabs on open and closed shapes (length, thickness, 3D tabs), Normal, Dog-Bone and T-Bone corner fillets, drilling with peck and dwell, true-shape nesting. https://docs.vectric.com/docs/V9.0/VCarvePro/ENU/Help/VCarvePro.pdf
- Laguna article on cabinet nesting: lock grain before nesting, limit rotation, respect vacuum zones for small parts near the sheet edge. https://info.lagunatools.com/optimize-cabinet-cnc-nesting-for-better-sheet-yield
- Other names seen, not studied in depth: Cabinet Vision, EZNESTING, MaxCut, Enroute, Microvellum.
- Caveat: most sources are vendor pages. Feature availability in current versions is not verified.

**Question 1: functions that a router CAM has and a milling CAM has not (one line each).**
1. True-shape nesting of parts on sheets (#2156, #2158 to #2166).
2. Grain direction on sheet and part, with rotation lock.
3. Grain continuity across adjacent parts (sequence match).
4. Tabs, onion skin, stay-down and small-part hold strategies.
5. Dogbone and T-bone corner relief.
6. Multi-spindle drill block with spindle selection.
7. Drill bank patterns (32 mm line bore) as one grouped operation.
8. Vacuum zones in the machine file and in the nest.
9. Sheet part labels with job data.
10. Remnant library.
11. Part priority by job or cabinet.
12. Pre- and post-tool-change macros for ATC and aggregate heads.
13. Cut-list import (part, quantity, material, grain).
14. Spoilboard surfacing.

Research answers, part 2: questions 4 to 7.

**Question 4: what the nesting issues do not cover for a router workflow.**
Covered already: true-shape placer with rotation modes `Locked`, `Orthogonal`, `FixedStep` (#2158); cut order (#2159); Nest entity (#2160); tabs, onion skin, vacuum small-before-large order, inside-corner warnings (#2161); UI (#2163); remnant sheets and waste export (#2164); MCP (#2165); 3D part instances (#2166). Machines and controllers: #1907, #1918.
Not covered:
- Grain direction as data on sheet and part. #2158 has a `Locked` mode but no grain field.
- Grain continuity across adjacent parts.
- Dogbone and T-bone relief. #2161 only warns about tight inside corners.
- Drill banks and multi-spindle heads.
- Vacuum zones as machine data. #2161 has an order rule only.
- Sheet labels.
- A remnant library that persists between jobs. #2164 covers one remnant sheet.
- Part priority by job or group.
- Tool-change macros for ATC and aggregate heads.
- Cut-list import.

**Question 5: grain.**
- Products set grain per material (sheet) and keep the grain direction of the part from its design. Source: https://www.goengineer.com/swood/nesting
- The nest obeys it with a rotation rule: fixed, or limited to 90 degree steps. Source: same page. Laguna advises to lock the grain before nesting. Source: https://info.lagunatools.com/optimize-cabinet-cnc-nesting-for-better-sheet-yield
- SigmaNEST has a part group that keeps grain consistent over a subset of parts. Source: https://www.globalspec.com/learnmore/industrial_engineering_software/engineering_scientific_software/nesting_software
- Grain continuity across adjacent parts is weak in products. MaxCut documents that separate parts are nested for yield only, and the user must combine the fronts into one panel. A newer MaxCut note mentions a Match Grain function. This is not verified. Sources: https://support.maxcutsoftware.com/hc/en-us/articles/360006652874-Can-I-optimise-drawer-fronts-to-have-grain-matching and https://knowledge.maxcutsoftware.com/doc/how-to-match-grain-in-maxcut
- Sequence matching in the trade means cutting adjacent doors from one panel in order. Source: https://vtindustries.com/webres/File/architectural-doors/Technical%20Bulletins/VT-Technical-Bulletin-P470-Matching-Faces-Between-a-Panel.pdf
- Proposal: a grain angle on the sheet, a grain angle and a "grain matters" flag on the part, and a rotation filter. Then a "match group" that places the parts of one group side by side in sequence on one sheet.

**Question 6: multi-spindle drill heads.**
- A drill block is an aggregate with many sub-spindles. The codes are machine and controller specific. No public standard exists. Source: https://forums.autodesk.com/t5/hsm-post-processor-forum/syntec-with-drill-block/td-p/10710447
- Public examples (forum level, not vendor documents): Syntec controllers select a drill with an M-code (M33 in one report) and tool numbers T21 to T29. One KOMO example uses tool numbers T301 to T311 with one work offset `G54 Pxx` for each spindle. One RhinoCAM example encodes the spindle set in a number and decodes it in the post (M88 for X-axis spindles, M89 for Y-axis spindles). Source: https://mecsoft.com/blog/rhinocams-programmable-post-processor/
- HOMAG describes heads with up to 45 spindles, vertical and horizontal groups, and a C axis. The NC word detail is not public in what I found. Source: https://www.homag.com/en/news-events/news/article/advanced-solutions-for-cnc-processing-and-drilling-technology-from-single-operation-to-interlinking-in-cells
- Thermwood nesting notes show drill banks of 3 and 5 spindles, custom bank counts and 32 mm line bores. Source: https://www.thermwood.com/updates_control_nesting_home.htm
- Conclusion: the machine file needs a list of spindles with an id, an XY offset, an axis group (X or Y row), a tool number and a fixed speed. The post needs a template for "select spindle set". Each controller needs its own public source. I could not verify any vendor manual. Open question for the maintainer: which router controller comes first.

**Question 7: other router functions.**
- Tabs, onion skin: all products have them. Tab drilling and 3D tabs exist. Covered in #2161 for nests. Single-part tabs are not an issue yet.
- Small-part hold-down: stay-down paths, spiral-inward cutting, small-first order (SigmaNEST, Mozaik pages above). #2161 covers the order only.
- Vacuum zones: Thermwood passes zone codes through machine code. Laguna says nests must respect zones.
- Sheet labels: barcode, part name, material (SWOOD, Mozaik).
- Remnants: Mozaik and SWOOD keep a library.
- Dogbone and T-bone: Vectric has Normal, Dog-Bone and T-Bone. CloudCut says automatic dogbones.
- Tool changes on an aggregate head: Thermwood has pre- and post-tool-change macros. The public pages do not describe aggregate-head tool changes in detail.

Research answers, part 3: question 8 (Router tab) and the sub-issues.

**Recommendation: do not add a Router tab. Use the machine type.**
- CamCraft already has machine kinds (`Kind` in the post crate: Mill, Lathe, MillTurn, Plasma, Waterjet, WireEdm). Add a Router kind, or a router flag on Mill, that shows router functions and hides the rest.
- Router functions are not one operation family. They are mostly sheet jobs (nest, labels, remnants, vacuum zones) and options on existing operations (tabs, dogbones, drill banks). A tab holds one family. These functions cut across families.
- Nesting already has its own tree node in #2163. The Nest entity can show only when the machine is a router or a 2D cutter. Waterjet and plasma use it too (#2156, #2161).
- Cloud and desktop router products show one job screen for sheet, nest and toolpaths. They do not split by a tab.
- A tab needs a new page layout, tests and icons for few unique operations. The machine kind gives the same result with less work.
- Question for the maintainer: "Do you want a Router machine kind that shows Nest and router options in the Milling tab, in place of a new Router tab?" My answer: yes.

Not filed: spoilboard surfacing (a facing operation covers it; check before a new issue), small-part hold strategies and tabs on nests (#2161 covers them), router machine data (#1907, #1918).
Not verified: vendor manuals for drill-block words, current-version features of all products, the 800 router claim of CloudCut.
Research complete. The Router tab decision waits for the maintainer.

The maintainer decided on 2026-11-17 (question dialog): no Router tab; a Router machine kind shows the router functions on the Milling tab. He also confirmed that the product he named is CloudCut (cloudcut.cam). The decision is recorded in https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/2410.
